content.title: About
content.content: Horchata is a traditional refreshing drink made from milk, rice, cinnamon and sugar. The milk‑based version gives the beverage a creamy texture and a gentle milky flavor while preserving the characteristic cinnamon aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Horchata originates from Mexico, where it is traditionally prepared with rice, almonds or tiger nuts.
Milk‑based horchata is often served chilled in hot weather as a cooling beverage.
Cinnamon and vanilla are classic flavorings, sometimes complemented with nutmeg.
In some regions coconut milk replaces cow’s milk, creating a tropical twist.
Horchata can be sweet or mildly spiced depending on the amount of sugar and spices used.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The milk used in the recipe is rich in calcium, which supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Rice and milk provide B1, B2 and B12 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential (when fermented)
items.content: If the horchata is fermented, beneficial bacteria develop, promoting gut health.

items.title: Low fat (when using skim milk)
items.content: Using skim milk makes the drink lower in calories while still providing protein.

items.title: Antioxidant effect of cinnamon
items.content: Cinnamon contains polyphenols that may help reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after drinking milk‑based horchata.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Traditional recipes contain a notable amount of sugar, which can increase calorie intake and affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins should avoid this beverage.

items.title: Excessive cinnamon
items.content: Large amounts of cinnamon may irritate the stomach in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Horchata can be enjoyed cold as a refreshing drink, paired with desserts, or used in cocktails. It can also be warmed and added to porridge or oatmeal for a creamy flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared horchata in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized containers.
